chapter: Family lore, Boston and Europe with Sam Price
title: First hearing brass; Garnett's influence
summary: Anna Mae first heard a brass band in Savannah; Eutris says he sneaked out from Morris Brown to the Roof Garden.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How about some of the brass instruments? Did you ever hear of anyone playing trumpets or trombones?
I never heard of it. The time I remember an instrument was when Jay C. came to New York.
You weren't living in Atlanta then.
It was in Savannah; Jay C. didn't have anything to do with that. That was another band...
Garnett played trombone when Jay was just a little boy. I think you were married and away then.
I left home kind of early.
When you left, you left from where?
From Social Circle, so that was before you moved to Atlanta?
Yes, before we moved there. You went to live with my sister. We had an older sister that was living in Savannah and she went down there to live with her.
There was two other sisters older, Stella and Emma. Jay, Walter, and Marion was at home then.

I used to hear bands in Savannah, you know, since I've thought about it. Had one good friend that was in a band. Blew some kind of horn, I don't know what it was, so that was the first time I ever heard brass.
Would you feel that Garnett kind of influenced Jay C. into wanting to play the trombone?

I'm sure he did, although he didn't want to because I really think that he was afraid that he might be a dropout in school. He didn't want him to do anything with his instrument but he was determined he was going to do it. He was in boarding school but we lived in the ( ? ) house just across from Morris Brown and he would come over and have his meals there most of the time. He would slip out of the school and come over to the ( ? ) house and get his horn and go to the Roof Garden. When he would come back he would come around to my window and knock and I would go and open the door and let him in. He was slipping in and out and my brother didn't know anything about it.
